indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.sub_strand: Data Collection, Organization, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis
indicator.content_standard: Create, label, and interpret line graphs to draw conclusions.
indicator.objective: Draw a line graph by determining the common attributes (title, axes and intervals) and draw the graph for a given table of values

skills.description: Identify title, axes, intervals for a line graph.
Plot points and join them to form a line graph.
Answer questions by reading a given line graph.

misconceptions: Joining points in the wrong order

questions.stem: A line graph shows temperature over time. What should the horizontal axis (x-axis) represent?
hints: The graph shows how temperature changes over something.
Time goes on the horizontal axis.
questions.explanation: The horizontal axis should be time.

questions.stem: What is the title of a line graph showing rainfall in Kumasi from January to June?
hints: The title tells what the graph is about.
It should include both place and topic.
questions.explanation: The title should be 'Rainfall in Kumasi'.

questions.stem: A table shows time (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 minutes) and temperature (20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 °C). What interval should be used on the horizontal axis?
hints: The time values increase by 1.
Use 1 unit per square for clarity.
questions.explanation: An interval of 1 minute per square fits the time values.
questions.misconception: Using 10 units per square, which would squash the graph.

questions.stem: The temperature values in a table range from 20°C to 70°C. What vertical interval would be suitable for the y-axis?
hints: The range is 50°C.
10°C intervals give 5 squares.
questions.explanation: 10°C per square is suitable for a range of 20 to 70.
questions.misconception: Using 1°C per square, which needs too many squares.

questions.stem: A line graph of water temperature over time has time on the x-axis and temperature on the y-axis. Which label is correct for the y-axis?
hints: The y-axis shows temperature.
Include the unit (°C).

questions.stem: A line graph has no title. What should be added?
options: A title describing what the graph shows
hints: Every graph needs a title.
The title tells the reader what the graph is about.
questions.explanation: Add a title that describes the data, e.g., 'Temperature of Water over Time'.

questions.stem: A table gives temperature at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 minutes. What is wrong with using an interval of 1 minute per square on the x-axis?
options: It wastes space because the data only uses even minutes
hints: The data values are 0, 2, 4, 6...
A 1-minute interval would leave empty columns.
questions.explanation: A 1-minute interval would leave unused squares; a 2-minute interval is better.

questions.stem: To plot (2, 30) on a graph, where do you start?
options: At 2 on the x-axis, then up 30 on the y-axis
At 30 on the x-axis, then up 2 on the y-axis
At the origin, then up 30 and left 2
At the origin, then right 30 and up 2
hints: The first number is the x-coordinate.
The second number is the y-coordinate.
questions.explanation: Start at 2 on the x-axis and move up to 30 on the y-axis.

questions.stem: A pupil plots the points (0,20), (1,30), (2,40), (3,50) but joins (1,30) to (3,50) directly, skipping (2,40). What is wrong?
options: The points must be joined in order
The graph should be a bar chart
hints: Line graphs join points in the order of the x-values.
Skipping a point breaks the pattern.
questions.explanation: Points must be joined in order of the x-values to show the trend correctly.
questions.misconception: Thinking the line can skip points.

questions.stem: Which point is 3 units right of (2, 30) and 10 units up?
hints: Right adds to x: 2+3=5.
Up adds to y: 30+10=40.

questions.stem: A line graph shows points at (0,10), (1,20), (2,30), (3,40). If the trend continues, what will the y-value be at x=5?
hints: Each step increases y by 10.
questions.explanation: The pattern adds 10 each time, so at x=5, y=60.

questions.stem: A pupil plots (0,20), (1,40), (2,60), (3,80) and joins them. What is the y-value at x=2?
hints: Look at the point with x=2.
The y-coordinate of (2,60) is 60.

questions.stem: A line graph shows temperature rising from 20°C at 0 min to 50°C at 3 min, then staying at 50°C from 3 to 6 min. What does the flat part of the graph mean?
hints: A flat line means no change in y.
The temperature stays the same.
questions.explanation: The flat part shows the temperature is constant at 50°C.
questions.misconception: Thinking a flat line means the graph is wrong.

questions.stem: A line graph shows temperature at 0 min = 15°C, 1 min = 25°C, 2 min = 35°C. What is the temperature at 1 min?
hints: Read the y-value when x=1.
The point is (1,25).

questions.stem: A line graph shows water temperature: 0 min = 20°C, 2 min = 30°C, 4 min = 40°C, 6 min = 50°C. After how many minutes does the temperature reach 40°C?
hints: Find the y-value 40°C.
Read the corresponding x-value.

questions.stem: A line graph shows temperature rising from 10°C at 0 min to 30°C at 2 min. What is the temperature at 1 min if the trend is steady?
hints: The temperature increases by 20°C over 2 min.
Halfway is 1 min, so halfway in temperature is ?
questions.explanation: 20°C + 20°C over 2 min means 10°C per min; at 1 min, 20°C.
questions.misconception: Choosing 15°C by halving the starting temperature.

questions.stem: A line graph shows temperature: 0 min = 15°C, 2 min = 25°C, 4 min = 35°C, 6 min = 45°C. What is the temperature at 5 min?
hints: The trend is a steady increase.
Between 4 and 6 min, halfway is 5 min.
questions.explanation: The temperature increases 10°C every 2 min, so at 5 min it is 40°C.

questions.stem: A line graph shows temperature reaching 70°C at 6 min. What was the temperature at 3 min if it started at 10°C and rose steadily?
hints: Rise from 10 to 70 over 6 min = 10°C per min.

questions.stem: A line graph shows temperature: 0 min = 20°C, 1 min = 30°C, 2 min = 40°C, 3 min = 50°C, then stays at 50°C from 3 to 5 min. What is the temperature at 4 min?
hints: The graph is flat from 3 to 5 min.
Flat means the temperature stays the same.
questions.explanation: The temperature stays at 50°C from 3 to 5 min, so at 4 min it is 50°C.
